subject: Derivative title carveouts & telemetry exception — next steps
messages:
From: Sam Cartwright <sam.cartwright@novum.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Novum Legal <legal@novum.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft amendment — derivative title & telemetry question

Hi Karthik / Ben,

Thanks for sending the order form earlier this week. Our legal team pushed back on two items that are blockers for us to finalize:

1) "Derivative title" language in Section 4 — Novum wants clarity that any model outputs customers adapt into their product are owned by Novum and that Redwood will not assert title over end-user-created derivatives. They proposed a carve-in instead of the current service-scope wording.

2) Telemetry / telemetry exception — we understand Redwood collects telemetry for reliability, but Novum is asking for an explicit exception preventing Redwood from using telemetry (including prompts/outputs) to improve models or train internal systems without an additional opt-in. They asked for an evidence log for any telemetry access.

I've attached the redline from our counsel (Novum_Amendment_20280810.docx) and highlighted the two asks. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a limited carveout for customer-owned derivatives and what we can offer on telemetry/feedback?

Best,
Sam
Sam Cartwright
Head of Platform, Novum AI

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft amendment — derivative title & telemetry question

Laura / Ben — forwarding Novum's note and their attached redline. High level: they want (a) stronger downstream title language and (b) a telemetry opt-out that prevents any training/quality improvement.

Quick thoughts:
- On derivative title: we typically offer "service outputs are customer data" + a limited feedback license so we can use anonymized telemetry to improve the service. We avoid broad assignments of title. Could we propose a clause that confirms customers own outputs they incorporate into their product but explicitly preserves Redwood's right to maintain/operate the service and to use aggregated, de-identified metrics?
- On telemetry: offering a full opt-out will impact our ability to fix regressions and may trigger a pricing uplift for customers who want strict non-use. We could propose a telemetry exception: Novum can opt-out of training/model-improvement use but agree to a narrow operations-only access (SRE/debugging) with audit trail.

Can you loop in legal on the specific language? I can coordinate a short call with Novum if helpful.

—Karthik

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft amendment — derivative title & telemetry question

Karthik — tagging in Legal counsel (internal) via this thread (will send offline redline suggestions to you and Ben). High-level positions we'd recommend:

1) Derivative title: counter with preservation of customer's rights to outputs they incorporate into a product (customer retains "output use rights") but refuse assignment of any "model derivative" or claims that would restrict Redwood from using patterns learned from anonymized, aggregated signals. Suggest language: "Customer retains rights to Customer Output for purposes of Productization; Redwood retains rights to models and aggregated, de-identified telemetry and metrics, and no transfer of model ownership shall occur."

2) Telemetry/feedback license: offer a two-tier option in the amendment:
   - Standard: Redwood may use de-identified/aggregated telemetry and Feedback (as defined) to improve models; operational logs used only for debugging are excluded from training datasets.
   - Locked: For an annual fee (pricing TBD), customer may opt into a "Locked Telemetry" plan that prevents any training use of telemetry/feedback. In that case Redwood will maintain an immutable access log and provide quarterly evidence reports.

We should draft both amendment options and present them to Novum so they can pick. This keeps our product improvements pipeline while offering a commercial path for strict privacy.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft amendment — derivative title & telemetry question

Agree with Laura. Two quick additions:
- We should quantify the cost delta for the Locked Telemetry plan before we present it — procurement will ask. Suggest +15–25% ARR depending on expected usage and retention requirements.
- On the outputs language, add an examples appendix that clarifies "customer-modified output" vs "model-internal artifacts" so Novum doesn't conflate usage with model IP. That appendix can be non-binding illustrative examples to keep drafting simple.

If you want, I can put a short pricing note together by Monday.

Ben

From: Sam Cartwright <sam.cartwright@novum.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Novum Legal <legal@novum.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft amendment — derivative title & telemetry question

Thanks for the quick responses. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- We don't want to block Redwood from operating the service, we just need written assurance that our downstream customers won't lose title if we incorporate outputs into our product. We can accept a definition of "Customer Output" that is limited to content created from our prompts and post-processed by our engineers.
- The Locked Telemetry option sounds promising but Novum needs specifics on what counts as "de-identified" vs "operational logs." Can you provide a short spec and an example report for the evidence logs?

Also, we prefer a quick 30-min call this week to align on the two-option approach rather than exchanging many redlines. Available Thu/Fri morning PST.

—Sam

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sam Cartwright <sam.cartwright@novum.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft amendment — derivative title & telemetry question

Sam — great, thanks. Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Laura & Legal to draft two short amendment options (Standard + Locked Telemetry) and a one-page appendix with concrete examples of "Customer Output" vs "Model Artifacts" (by EOD Wed).
2) Ben to send a draft pricing delta for Locked Telemetry and any operational support fees (by Mon EOD).
3) Karthik to set a 30-min alignment call with Novum for Thu 10:00 AM PST (sending calendar invite now).
4) Provide Novum with a 1-page evidence-log template showing access events, fields captured, and retention policy (ops/infra to produce stub).

I've attached the quick redline we started (redlines-msav2.pdf) to show the minimal tweaks we think will resolve their asks without broad IP transfer. If that timeline works, I will bring Legal on the call and we can aim to close the amendment and get the order form signed within two weeks.

Thanks all — I'll circulate the invite and doc links in a follow-up.

—Karthik
